# Request payload silently dropped when retransmitting Uri-Path-Abbrev requests (coap_net.c)

**ID:** vuln-0001
**Severity:** LOW
**Found:** 2026-11-17 11:11:21 UTC
**Target:** libcoap 4.3.5 (source snapshot)
**Endpoint:** coap_send() → coap_net.c (Uri-Path-Abbrev expansion path)
**Method:** CoAP (UDP datagram generated by the library)
**CVSS:** 3.7
**Confidence:** High
**Fix Effort:** Trivial

## Description

When a CoAP session has learned that the peer does not understand the Uri-Path-Abbrev option, `coap_send()` rebuilds outgoing requests with the abbreviation expanded. The rebuilt PDU is created correctly, but the original message payload is appended to the *old* PDU, which is then freed, so the request that reaches the wire carries no payload. Any body-bearing PUT/POST issued on such a session is delivered to the server without its content.

## Evidence

Vulnerable build: the transmitted datagram contains the expanded path options but no payload marker and no `BODY`:

```
WARN coap_add_data: PDU already contains data
wire bytes: 4103e19661b1610162e4000c452e497b
payload present: NO (payload lost)
```

Decoded: `41 03` (CON PUT), token `61`, `b1 61` (Uri-Path "a"), `01 62` (Uri-Path "b"), `e4 ...` (remaining options) — the message ends without the `0xFF` payload marker.

Corrected build (`coap_add_data(new, ...)`): the payload follows the options:

```
wire bytes: 41037df061b1610162e4000c70293493ff424f4459
payload present: YES
```

Library debug trace of the same send on the vulnerable build, showing the expansion path ran and the payload was appended to the discarded PDU:

```
DEBG *  Retransmitting PDU with Uri-Path-Abbrev replaced (3)
DEBG *  127.0.0.1:40065 <-> 127.0.0.1:46375 UDP : netif: sent   16 bytes
v:1 t:CON c:PUT i:af07 {61} [ Uri-Path:a, Uri-Path:b, Request-Tag:0x2230ebec ]
```

versus the corrected build:

```
DEBG *  127.0.0.1:40065 <-> 127.0.0.1:46375 UDP : netif: sent   21 bytes
v:1 t:CON c:PUT i:3139 {61} [ Uri-Path:a, Uri-Path:b, Request-Tag:0x1f04c5c1 ] :: 'BODY'
```

## Impact

Integrity of client requests is silently altered: a request issued with content is transmitted without any content. For a resource whose handler treats an empty body as "replace with nothing" (or which deletes on empty PUT), the effect is data loss on the server; for any other handler the request semantics change without the application being informed. In a proxy chain the truncated request is relayed upstream as-is, so the same loss propagates. No confidentiality or availability impact was demonstrated.

## Counterevidence

Looked for a reason the payload might legitimately be re-added elsewhere: `coap_pdu_duplicate_lkd()` documents and implements "token and options only" (no data), so no other code path restores it; the sibling implementation at `src/coap_block.c:5197` adds the payload to the duplicated PDU, which produces a correct request. Considered whether the data might already live inside the duplicate: it does not, and the observed wire bytes on the vulnerable build contain no payload. Considered whether the path is unreachable: it requires libcoap block mode plus the Uri-Path-Abbrev feature (a library API not used by the shipped examples), which limits exposure; that constraint is reflected in the attack complexity and in the low severity, but it does not make the behaviour intended. No memory-safety consequence was observed, only loss of the payload.

## What Would Change This Severity

If Uri-Path-Abbrev were in common use (or enabled by default for body-bearing requests), or if a downstream resource treated an empty PUT as a destructive "clear" operation, the demonstrated silent data loss would raise the integrity impact and with it the severity.

## Technical Analysis

`coap_send_internal()` contains a fallback for peers that rejected the Uri-Path-Abbrev option. Once `session->no_path_abbrev` is set (it is set by the library when the server answers `4.02 Bad Option` to an abbreviated request), every subsequent request carrying a Uri-Path-Abbrev option is duplicated with `coap_pdu_duplicate_lkd(..., COAP_BOOL_TRUE)`, which expands the abbreviation into Uri-Path options. That function explicitly copies only the token and options, not the payload:

```c title=coap_pdu.c startLineNumber=233 endLineNumber=235
/*
 * Note: This does not include any data, just the token and options
 */
```

The payload therefore has to be re-added to the *new* PDU. The code instead appends it to the source PDU:

```c title=src/coap_net.c startLineNumber=1802 endLineNumber=1808
      new = coap_pdu_duplicate_lkd(pdu, session, pdu->actual_token.length,
                                   pdu->actual_token.s, NULL, COAP_BOOL_TRUE);
      if (new) {
        if (coap_get_data(pdu, &data_len, &data)) {
          coap_add_data(pdu, data_len, data);
        }
        coap_log_debug("*  Retransmitting PDU with Uri-Path-Abbrev replaced (3)\n");
        coap_delete_pdu_lkd(pdu);
        pdu = new;
```

`pdu` is the PDU that is deleted two lines later, so the data is written to freed-and-discarded storage, while `new` (the PDU that is actually transmitted) never receives a payload. The call also emits `coap_add_data: PDU already contains data`, because the source PDU already held that payload.

The identical construct elsewhere in the library writes to the new PDU and is correct, confirming the intended behaviour:

```c title=src/coap_block.c startLineNumber=5191 endLineNumber=5199
          pdu = coap_pdu_duplicate_lkd(lg_crcv->sent_pdu, session, ltoken_len,
                                       ltoken, NULL, COAP_BOOL_TRUE);
        if (pdu) {
          if (coap_get_data(lg_crcv->sent_pdu, &data_len, &data)) {
            coap_add_data(pdu, data_len, data);
          }
```

Reachability: the fallback runs only for sessions where the library's block layer is active (`session->block_mode & COAP_BLOCK_USE_LIBCOAP`) and `session->no_path_abbrev` has been set, which requires the application to use the Uri-Path-Abbrev facility (`coap_path_into_optlist_abbrev()` / `coap_uri_into_optlist_abbrev()` with a mapping). A remote CoAP server (or an on-path attacker able to rewrite server responses) can force the transition by answering `4.02` to the first abbreviated request, after which every abbreviated body-bearing request from that client is silently sent without its payload.

## Proof of Concept

1. Bind a local UDP socket to act as the upstream CoAP server and note its port.
2. Create a libcoap client session to that port with `COAP_BLOCK_USE_LIBCOAP` enabled and `session->no_path_abbrev = 1`, which is the state the library itself enters after the server answers `4.02` to a Uri-Path-Abbrev request.
3. Register a Uri-Path-Abbrev mapping (`coap_upa_server_mapping()`), then build a `PUT` with one Uri-Path-Abbrev option and the 4-byte payload `BODY`, and pass it to `coap_send()`.
4. Read the datagram that the library actually transmitted.
5. Observe that the abbreviated option has been expanded to `Uri-Path: a`, `Uri-Path: b`, but the message ends after the options: there is no `0xFF` payload marker and no `BODY`, so the payload was lost.

Running the same program against a library with `coap_add_data(new, ...)` at the reported line shows the payload present (`... 0x0c 0x70 0x29 0x34 0x93 0xff 'B''O''D''Y'`).

```c
#include "coap3/coap_internal.h"
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <arpa/inet.h>
#include <sys/socket.h>
#include <unistd.h>

int main(void) {
  int rx;
  struct sockaddr_in sin;
  socklen_t slen = sizeof(sin);
  coap_context_t *ctx;
  coap_session_t *session;
  coap_address_t dst;
  coap_pdu_t *pdu;
  uint8_t buf[1500];
  ssize_t n;
  static coap_upa_abbrev_t map[] = { { 1, "a/b" } };

  /* local receiver standing in for the upstream CoAP server */
  rx = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_DGRAM, 0);
  memset(&sin, 0, sizeof(sin));
  sin.sin_family = AF_INET;
  sin.sin_addr.s_addr = htonl(INADDR_LOOPBACK);
  sin.sin_port = 0;
  bind(rx, (struct sockaddr *)&sin, sizeof(sin));
  getsockname(rx, (struct sockaddr *)&sin, &slen);

  coap_startup();
  ctx = coap_new_context(NULL);
  coap_address_init(&dst);
  dst.addr.sin = sin;
  dst.size = sizeof(sin);
  session = coap_new_client_session(ctx, NULL, &dst, COAP_PROTO_UDP);
  session->state = COAP_SESSION_STATE_ESTABLISHED;
  /* state reached after the server answered 4.02 to a Uri-Path-Abbrev request */
  session->block_mode |= COAP_BLOCK_USE_LIBCOAP;
  session->no_path_abbrev = 1;
  coap_upa_server_mapping(map, 1);

  pdu = coap_pdu_init(COAP_MESSAGE_CON, COAP_REQUEST_CODE_PUT,
                      coap_new_message_id(session), 1152);
  coap_add_token(pdu, 1, (const uint8_t *)"a");
  coap_add_option(pdu, COAP_OPTION_URI_PATH_ABB, 1, (const uint8_t *)"\x01");
  coap_add_data(pdu, 4, (const uint8_t *)"BODY");
  coap_send(session, pdu);

  n = recv(rx, buf, sizeof(buf), 0);
  if (n < 0) { perror("recv"); return 2; }
  printf("wire bytes: ");
  for (ssize_t i = 0; i < n; i++) printf("%02x", buf[i]);
  printf("\npayload present: %s\n",
         memmem(buf, (size_t)n, "BODY", 4) ? "YES" : "NO (payload lost)");
  close(rx);
  return 0;
}
```

## Code Analysis

**Location 1:** `src/coap_net.c` (line 1805)
  Copy the request payload into the duplicated PDU instead of the discarded source PDU
  ```
            coap_add_data(pdu, data_len, data);
  ```

  **Suggested Fix:**
```diff
-           coap_add_data(pdu, data_len, data);
+           coap_add_data(new, data_len, data);
```

**Location 2:** `src/coap_block.c` (line 5197)
  Informational: the equivalent block-layer fallback correctly adds the payload to the duplicated PDU (there `pdu` is the new PDU)
  ```
              coap_add_data(pdu, data_len, data);
  ```

## Remediation

Add the request payload to the duplicated PDU that is actually transmitted, not to the source PDU that is deleted immediately afterwards. The duplicated PDU deliberately carries only the token and options, so the payload must be re-added explicitly after the duplication succeeds and before the source PDU is released. Consider adding a regression test that sends a body-bearing request through the Uri-Path-Abbrev fallback and asserts the payload arrives, since no existing unit test covers this branch.

## Fix Verification

Security closure: rebuilt the library with only `src/coap_net.c` changed (`coap_add_data(new, ...)`), recompiled the PoC against the rebuilt archive, and re-ran it. Before the change the transmitted datagram is `4103e19661b1610162e4000c452e497b` (no payload marker, no `BODY`); after the change it is `41037df061b1610162e4000c70293493ff424f4459` (`0xFF` payload marker followed by `BODY`), and the `coap_add_data: PDU already contains data` warning no longer appears. The trace now shows `:: 'BODY'` on the sent PDU.

Bypass review: re-read the diff independently of the analysis that produced it. `coap_get_data(pdu, &data_len, &data)` runs before `coap_add_data(new, ...)`, so `data` still points into the live source PDU while the bytes are copied into `new`; `coap_pdu_duplicate_lkd()` performs a deep copy of option values, and `coap_add_data()` copies the payload, so no pointer into the freed source survives. The payload is added only when the duplicate succeeded, so the `new == NULL` path (unknown abbreviation value, which returns NULL after freeing the duplicate) is unchanged. Checked the sibling call sites of the same pattern: `src/coap_block.c:5197` already targets the duplicated PDU, and `src/coap_net.c` has no other occurrence of this construct. Alternate input classes considered: zero-length payload (`coap_get_data()` returns 0 and nothing is added, unchanged), payload larger than one block (the block layer performs its own correct re-duplication), non-block-mode sessions (the branch is not reached), and sessions where the abbreviation value is not in the mapping table (the duplicate returns NULL, so the send proceeds unexpanded and the payload is untouched).

Preserved behaviour: requests without a Uri-Path-Abbrev option are not affected (the option lookup guards the block), and sessions that never set `no_path_abbrev` bypass the branch entirely, so normal token/option/payload handling is untouched. Ran the project's full unit-test suite against the patched library: 17 suites, 201 tests, 1500 assertions, 0 failures (same result as the unpatched build).

Repository checks: the changed line was compiled with the same flags as the rest of the library and the recompiled archive was linked into both the PoC and the unit-test driver; both link and run cleanly under AddressSanitizer/UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer with no diagnostics. Gap: no test in the suite exercises this branch, so the demonstration and the fixed-versus-unfixed wire comparison are the verification rather than a repository test.

## Assumptions

The embedding application uses the Uri-Path-Abbrev facility (a mapping registered via coap_upa_client_fallback()/coap_uri_into_optlist_abbrev()) and enables libcoap block mode. The session must have entered the `no_path_abbrev` state, which a server triggers by answering `4.02 Bad Option` to an abbreviated request. The shipped example programs do not use Uri-Path-Abbrev, so they are not affected.
